text: Municipal census from 1847 lists seventeen residents of a house with only three rooms. Final entry notes: The Hendersons live in the walls between Tuesday and Wednesday.

Marginalia discovered in a 1203 psalter: The angels have been on strike since Michaelmas. All miracles this season are performed by understudies. The handwriting matches no known scribe but appears in fortythree manuscripts across Europe.

Weather station data from 1934: Temperature recorded as nostalgic for six consecutive days in February. Barometric pressure readings replaced with childhood addresses. Local newspaper reported it as unseasonably memorable.

Entry 1956B: Patient's Xray reveals skeletal system belongs to different person entirely. Bone structure matches missing archaeologist from 1923 expedition. Patient has no knowledge of archaeology and was born in 1945.

Excavation in Mesopotamia, 2400 BCE site, recovered cuneiform tablet describing standardized time zones. Text includes phrase spring forward, fall back in protoAkkadian. Daylight saving time was not invented until 1916.

Digital anomaly: Library catalog system spontaneously generates call numbers for books that were never written. Patrons successfully check out these nonexistent volumes. Return dates are always yesterday.

Botanical survey 1891: Specimen of Quercus temporalis collected in Yorkshire. Tree rings indicate 400 years of growth completed in single afternoon. Acorns germinate into fully mature oaks instantaneously upon planting.
Census data from the Great Mice Revolution of 1603 lists seventeen human casualties and 40,000 rodent knights. The revolution succeeded. No subsequent records explain why we remember it differently.

Marginalia discovered in 14th century psalter: The cathedral dreams of flying south for winter. Architectural survey confirms NotreDame de Paris shifts 3.2 degrees southward each October, returns by spring.
